<reason>B more convincingly separates English’s communication benefits from institutional penalties against local-language knowledge. A explains network effects but does not establish that strengthening other languages would dismantle connectivity or degrade translation. B also answers the destruction challenge honestly: exclusion and diminished scientific function matter before extinction. A repeatedly treats remediable harms as causally unrelated to dominance, without defending that inference. B’s evidence for the overall scale of cultural loss remains less developed than its causal account, making this a clear but competitive win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal targets “fixable harms versus irreplaceable goods”: local-language scholarship can retain recognition while English translations reach international readers. This preserves the network while reducing hierarchy, exposing A’s unsupported leap from concentrated readership to necessary institutional subordination.</best_rebuttal>
